content: Health-promoting schools (HPS) are increasingly recognized as essential environments for fostering the health, development, and well-being of children and adolescents. These schools not only enhance long-term educational outcomes but also support the health and well-being of students, their families, and the broader community. The interconnected relationship between health and education extends far beyond formal schooling, emphasizing the importance of integrating health promotion into educational systems. A health-promoting school is defined as one that continuously strengthens its capacity to serve as a healthy environment for living, learning, and working. This concept adopts a whole-school approach, leveraging the organizational potential of schools to create physical, social-emotional, and psychological conditions conducive to both health and positive educational outcomes. By doing so, HPS initiatives benefit individuals, families, and communities alike. The implementation of HPS has been a global effort for decades, with widespread acknowledgment of its necessity for sustainability. To institutionalize health promotion within education systems, it is essential to integrate it into governance, resource allocation, educator training, information systems, and performance management. In 2018, the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNESCO launched an initiative to make every school a health-promoting school, developing global standards and indicators to guide implementation. This initiative aligns with other global efforts, such as the Sustainable Development Goals and public health emergency responses like the COVID-19 pandemic. The global standards for HPS provide a vision for schools worldwide to enhance the health, well-being, and educational outcomes of their students and communities. These standards advocate for a shift from isolated health programs to a comprehensive, whole-school approach that integrates health promotion into the school’s culture, conditions, and curriculum. The eight global standards for sustainable HPS systems emphasize government commitment, school policies, leadership, community partnerships, health services, and supportive environments. The implementation guidance for HPS is designed to assist governments at all levels in developing, planning, funding, and monitoring sustained whole-school approaches to health promotion. It aims to establish structures and mechanisms for adopting global standards and embedding them within the education sector. This guidance promotes leadership within the education sector and intersectoral collaboration to achieve health and well-being in schools. It also provides practical strategies and lessons aligned with the global standards to help governments determine what actions to take, how to implement them, and who should be involved. The implementation process follows a five-step cycle: establishing a shared understanding of HPS, conducting a situational analysis to identify priorities and stakeholders, developing a comprehensive plan, implementing the plan, and monitoring progress while identifying areas for improvement. The guidance also highlights the importance of inclusivity and equity in HPS implementation, ensuring that all members of the school community are involved in the design, management, and operations of health-promoting activities. Special attention is given to disadvantaged students, those with disabilities, and individuals who may not conform to conventional norms related to gender, sexuality, or reproductive health. Governance systems for HPS must be embedded within the education sector, with collaborative leadership at national, subnational, and local levels. Effective governance requires partnerships and coordination among stakeholders in education, health, and related sectors. A whole-school approach is essential, integrating health promotion into all aspects of schooling, including policies, infrastructure, curricula, and community engagement. Meaningful engagement of students, parents, and caregivers is critical for successful HPS implementation. Empowering children and adolescents, particularly girls, as agents of change can positively influence lifelong learning, development, and well-being. In summary, the global initiative to make every school a health-promoting school provides a comprehensive framework for integrating health and education. By adopting the global standards and following the implementation guidance, schools can create environments that support the health, well-being, and educational success of their students and communities.
